evidence: Static row; verified by parsing the frozen TOML, no runtime measurement is needed or claimed. Dimension weights: tests/scoring.toml:5-8 functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml (diff clean) and to the delivery profile in SKILL.md:28; gates at 0.0 (scoring.toml:1-3) and functional floor 0.05 (scoring.toml:10-11). No weight key in any [judge] block (keys are only isolated, judge, mcp_servers, mode, prompt_template, timeout in all five judge.toml files). Maximum contribution of the non-functional dimensions is 0.40 against 0.60 for functional, and score.py:107-109 zeroes the reward unless functional > 0.05, so style cannot outweigh function at dimension level. Per-criterion weights: functional has 38 binary criteria summing to 54.0 (12 at 1.0, 20 at 1.5, 6 at 2.0), spread max/min 2x. The tiers track what each criterion proves: 1.0 for single-mechanism basics that everything else already depends on (typing/join judge.toml:27, caret navigation :36, grapheme :45, mouse selection :54, find wrap :135, html preview :216, error line :225); 1.5 for conjunctions with atomic undo, concurrency, persistence or isolation (restart :306, stale save :315/:324, history :333, isolation :288, dynamic code :297); 2.0 only for the deepest multi-state outcomes that the brief leads with (multi-caret atomic burst :99, same-line carets :117, JS format semantics+undo :189, last-good recovery :252, stop cancels pending work :270, live update keeps editing state :351). Cluster totals are proportionate to the public brief (instruction.md:1 'the editor itself matters ... format it, make changes in several places ... without losing a draft when another tab saves first'): core editing 9.0, multi-caret 5.5, find/replace 5.0, colouring 2.5, format 4.5, run/recovery 12.0, preview boundary 3.0, persistence/history/multi-tab 12.5. The only presentation-like functional items, syntax colouring (:171 at 1.5, :180 at 1.0), are 4.6 percent of the functional dimension and are a stated requirement (ui.md:13). Polish (6 binary, all 1.0) and visual (3 likert points=5, all 1.0) are uniform, so no craft item is privileged inside its dimension. Weak-app probe: a handsome shell whose editor accepts text and runs but implements nothing else earns at most about 0.4 plus a few percent and only if it clears the floor; a plain but fully working app earns at least 0.6, so the order is preserved. Conforming-alternative probe: no weight depends on a golden-specific choice. Observation recorded, not a defect of this row: because dimension shares are template-fixed and the hardening raised functional to 38 criteria, the reward share of one item is 1.11-2.22 percent for a functional criterion, 3.33 percent for a polish criterion and 6.67 percent for a visual likert criterion, so e.g. cw_undo_redo_availability (polish/judge.toml:45-48) carries twice cw_undo_restores_caret (functional/judge.toml:124-126) and one visual criterion (visual/judge.toml:48-52) exceeds save/restart plus stale-save plus history together (5.0 percent). This follows from the mandated 0.6/0.2/0.2 policy and the 38:6:3 criterion counts, cannot be changed without altering shared scoring policy, and does not let style outweigh function in aggregate. No configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index.json scope: scripted golden only), so the reward-ordering runtime evidence owned by rows 40/42 remains unmeasured; this row does not rely on it.
